mem.t: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

lessons.title: Your Kingdom Come
lessons.theme: To pray for the kingdom is to ask God to reign in my life

v: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”

lessons.still: Slowly say the first three lines of the Lord’s Prayer. Pause at “Let your Kingdom come,” and quietly ask the Lord, “Lord, which corner of my life are you not yet reigning over today?”
teach: A kingdom has three elements: a king, subjects and territory. God’s kingdom is the same: God is the King, believers are his subjects, and the territory is wherever God reigns, from one heart, to one home, to one city. To pray “Your kingdom come” is to ask God to extend his reign to more and more places.

The first words of Jesus’ public ministry were: “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.” To repent is to turn from ruling ourselves to letting God rule. The first three requests of the Lord’s Prayer flow together: hallowing his name, the coming of his kingdom, his will being done on earth as in heaven. In heaven, God’s will is done without hindrance; we ask that it be so on earth too.

This prayer begins with me. I cannot pray “Your kingdom come” while insisting on being king in my own life. The first territory the kingdom claims is my heart. A shift in mindset: God’s kingdom is not only heaven in the future; it is God’s reign beginning in my life today.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God’s kingdom system is bringing the Lord’s Prayer to fulfilment. Letting Jesus reign is the heart of the kingdom; letting Jesus receive all the glory is its purpose. All the practices of this year have really been answering one prayer: Your kingdom come.
q: Who is God? — God is King. What does that mean for your life today?
Who am I? — Are you a subject of his kingdom, or still a king in your own little kingdom?
How shall I respond? — Into which corner of your life will you let God’s reign extend today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “If I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.” The kingdom is not just an idea; it came in concrete form in Jesus: the sick were healed, captives were set free, sinners were forgiven.
lessons.pray: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. Let your kingdom come, and let it come first in my heart. Let your will be done in my home, my work and my relationships as it is in heaven. Reign in every corner of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Begin and end today with the Lord’s Prayer
Write down one area of your life where you are still “playing king”
Pray for God’s kingdom to come in your city and your nation
lessons.noon: “Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven” — Lord, right now reign in me.

lessons.title: Seek First His Kingdom
lessons.theme: Put the kingdom first, and everything else will find its place

v: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

lessons.still: Name your worries one by one: food, drink, clothing, work, family, the future. After each one, add, “My heavenly Father knows.” Finally, say quietly, “I seek your kingdom first.”
teach: Fill a jar: first the big rocks, then the pebbles, then the sand, and finally the water, and everything fits. Pour in the sand first, and the big rocks will not go in. Life is the same: put in what matters most first, and the rest will find its place. “Seek first his kingdom” is the big rock of life.

Jesus does not say that food, drink and clothing are unimportant. He says, “your heavenly Father knows.” Worry is rooted in thinking everything depends on us. The Gentiles chase after these things because they do not know the Father; God’s children can seek his kingdom and his righteousness first, because the Father takes responsibility for “all these things.” “First” is not only about time; it is about the order of priorities in our hearts.

Seeking the kingdom first is very concrete. With our time: give God the first part of the day. With our money: set aside what is holy first. When making decisions: first ask, “Will this extend God’s kingdom?” In relationships: God first, then ourselves, then people, then tasks. A shift in mindset: from “I’ll look after myself first and then serve God” to “I’ll seek God first, and God will surely look after me.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships (God first, then ourselves, then people, then tasks) is the everyday version of “seek first his kingdom.” It is the order of priorities that lets Jesus reign, and in an anxious age it is the secret of living from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself.
q: Who is God? — “Your heavenly Father knows.” How does this help you face your worries?
Who am I? — What is currently the “big rock” in the jar of your life?
How shall I respond? — Tomorrow, how will you concretely seek his kingdom “first”?
lessons.jesus: At the well Jesus told his disciples, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work.” He could even set aside a meal, because the Father’s kingdom was his most satisfying food. He lived out a life that seeks the kingdom first.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, you know everything I need. I hand my worries over to you and choose to seek your kingdom and your righteousness first. Rearrange the priorities of my life so that you come first, and let everything else find its place in your hands. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make prayer the first thing you do when you wake tomorrow
Write down one worry, and next to it write, “My heavenly Father knows”
Before making a decision, ask, “Will this extend God’s kingdom?”
lessons.noon: “But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness” — Lord, right now you are my first.

lessons.title: Establishing God’s Domain on Earth
lessons.theme: The kingdom is like yeast, quietly changing the whole from small beginnings

v: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took, and sowed in his field,
which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”
He spoke another parable to them. “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”
for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

lessons.still: Imagine your home, your office or your small group as a lump of dough, and yourself as a small piece of yeast the Lord has placed in it. Quietly say, “Lord, let your life spread out slowly through me.”
teach: Drop a single drop of ink into a glass of clear water. At first it is just a small dark spot, but soon the whole glass is coloured. The kingdom’s influence does not come through noise or force but through permeation and transformation: quiet yet persistent, small yet real.

The parable of the mustard seed speaks of the kingdom’s expansion: from the smallest of seeds to a tree where birds come to roost. The parable of the yeast speaks of the kingdom’s permeation: hidden in the dough until the whole batch is leavened. Paul explains the kingdom’s essence: it is “not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.” The kingdom is not a building or an organisation; it is the quality of life that God’s reign brings.

Establishing God’s domain on earth means letting righteousness, peace and joy flow out wherever God has placed us: home, workplace, neighbourhood, church. This is the very heart behind the six areas of the life-practice courses: spiritual life, marriage, family, church, work and social life. Each one is kingdom territory. Wherever you are, that is where the kingdom begins.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose: to build God’s kingdom system. God’s kingdom system is not about moving the world into the church, but about bringing God’s reign into every corner of the world. A changed life changes our way of living; a changed way of living changes our relationships; changed relationships change our ministry.
q: Who is God? — God chooses to work in small ways, like a mustard seed and yeast. What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Are you that piece of yeast where you are?
How shall I respond? — This week, into which area of life will you bring righteousness, peace or joy?
lessons.jesus: Jesus spent thirty-some years on earth, most of them living and working in the small town of Nazareth. He was in no hurry to build a vast organisation. Instead he sowed the seed of the kingdom in villages, in homes and among a small band of disciples, and that seed has now grown into a great tree that fills the earth.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for placing me in my family, my workplace and my community as your yeast. Let your righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit spread out slowly from my life. May your kingdom begin to come right where I am. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose one area of your life and write down one kingdom quality you will bring into it
Do one thing at work or at home that promotes justice or peace
Pray specifically for a neighbour or colleague
lessons.noon: “God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit” — Lord, right now let your kingdom spread out through me.

lessons.title: The Kingdom, the Power and the Glory Are God’s
lessons.theme: The kingdom, the power and the glory all belong to God, not to me

v: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
For of him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.

lessons.still: Cup your hands as though you were holding a crown. Think of the power, reputation and achievements you have sought for yourself, and place them all on this crown. Then slowly lift it up and offer it to the Lord who sits on the throne.
teach: At an awards ceremony, a winner steps onto the stage, and his first words are thanks to the teachers and team who trained him. The most moving moment is not when he raises the trophy, but when he turns the honour toward others. In God’s kingdom this is not mere courtesy but the truth: everything belonged to God all along.

The risen Jesus declares, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” The authority is his, not ours; we only act in his name. After marvelling at God’s wonderful plan of salvation, Paul ends in praise: “For of him, through him, and to him are all things.” From source, through process, to goal, it is all God. That is why the Lord’s Prayer closes with “for yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory.”

The greatest danger in building God’s kingdom system is that, as we go on building, it quietly turns into building “my system.” When ministry bears fruit, numbers grow and our reputation spreads, self-rule creeps back onto the throne. So after every victory we must return to this prayer: yours is the kingdom, yours is the power, yours is the glory.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The two cores: let Jesus reign (the kingdom and the power are his), and let Jesus receive all the glory (the glory is his). Pride is grasping power; humility is laying it down. Giving the kingdom, the power and the glory back to God is humility at its most complete.
q: Who is God? — “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” What does this show you about the risen Lord?
Who am I? — In your service or achievements, is there glory you have quietly kept for yourself?
How shall I respond? — Which achievement or position of power will you concretely give back to the Lord?
lessons.jesus: When the crowd wanted to make Jesus king by force, he withdrew to the mountain alone. He performed many miracles, yet he said, “I don’t seek my own glory.” He gave all the glory to the Father, and the Father highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, all authority in heaven and on earth is yours; all things are of you, through you and to you. I lay down the power and reputation I have wanted to grasp, and I lay every achievement before your throne. Yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, for ever. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Look back on one fruit of your service this year, and offer God thanks and glory for it
Publicly honour the work of someone who serves behind the scenes
Each time you finish a task, pray silently, “Glory to you.”
lessons.noon: “To him be the glory for ever!” — Lord, right now all the glory belongs to you.

lessons.title: Ready for the Lord’s Return
lessons.theme: The gospel goes to all the world, and the bride makes herself ready for the Bridegroom

v: This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
He who testifies these things says, “Yes, I am coming soon.” Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus!

lessons.still: Quietly say, “Come, Lord Jesus!” Repeat it three times, each time more slowly and more sincerely. Then ask yourself: if the Lord came back today, would my heart be ready?
teach: A bride who knows her bridegroom is coming for her does not stare anxiously at the clock all day. She prepares with joy: getting her things in order, making herself beautiful, letting family and friends know. Expectation brings not fear but hope with a direction.

Jesus said, “This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.” The Lord’s return is closely tied to the spread of the gospel. At the very end of the Bible, the Lord promises, “I come quickly,” and the church answers, “Come, Lord Jesus!” This is the completion of the kingdom prayer: the coming of the kingdom will be fully realised when the King returns.

This week we have moved from Your kingdom come (Day 1), seek first his kingdom (Day 2), establishing God’s domain (Day 3) and glory to God (Day 4) to today’s readiness for the Lord’s return. Next week is the final week of the year. We will look back on this year’s grace and be sent out to become spiritual parents to others, ready for the great revival of the last days.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God’s kingdom system is ultimately about preparing the bride to meet the Bridegroom. Multiplication is not about growing the size of the church but about taking the gospel to the whole world. Living in the hope of the Lord’s return means making him King today.
q: Who is God? — What does the promise “I come quickly” show you about this faithful Lord?
Who am I? — Is your attitude to the Lord’s return one of unfamiliarity, fear or longing?
How shall I respond? — Before the Lord returns, who will you share the gospel with?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus ascended, the angels said, “This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.” The Lord who died, rose and ascended for us will surely come again. He is the beginning and the end.
lessons.pray: Come, Lord Jesus! Until you return, make me like a bride who is ready, waiting with joy and faithfully proclaiming you. May the good news of the kingdom go out from my lips, and may the people around me be ready to meet you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the name of someone you want to share the gospel with before the Lord returns
End every prayer today with “Come, Lord Jesus”
Share with a spiritual companion what the Lord’s return means for your life today
lessons.noon: “Yes, come” — Lord, right now I make my heart ready to welcome you.
